title: Parliamentary system of government
competency: Define the parliamentary system and its features.

keywords.def: The relationship between the executive and the legislature: parliamentary or presidential.
A system where the executive (prime minister and cabinet) comes from and is accountable to the parliament.
In a parliamentary country, the ceremonial head, such as a president or monarch.
The holder of real executive power, such as the prime minister in a parliamentary country.

en.text: A system of government is how the executive and the legislature relate. In a parliamentary system, voters elect the parliament; the party or coalition with most seats forms the government, and the prime minister leads it and is accountable to parliament. The head of state is ceremonial. Features: leadership of the PM, nominal head of state, political homogeneity, collective responsibility and fusion of powers. Ethiopia is parliamentary.

screens.title: Systems of government
paras: A system of government is the relationship between the executive and legislative branches.
Presidential: the people elect the executive and legislature separately.
Parliamentary: the executive is selected from the legislature.
In Ethiopia voters elect the House of Peoples' Representatives; the prime minister is chosen from it.

screens.title: How it works
paras: The party or coalition with most seats in parliament forms the government.
The prime minister leads the cabinet and is accountable to parliament.
He or she can be removed when parliament loses confidence.
In Ethiopia, Article 74/2 lets ministers come from either House or from qualified non-members.
table: The PM leads the majority party
screens.note: Parliamentary countries: Ethiopia, Denmark, Japan, Malaysia, Sweden, Germany, India, Italy, Pakistan, Botswana, South Africa, the UK, where the system began.
